claims.claim: Born 17 February 1963 in Tainan, Taiwan; 63 years old in October 2026 (intro, summary, FAQ, facts.birthDate/birthPlace)
claims.note: Britannica gives 17 Feb 1963, Tainan. CHM gives 1963, Tainan, without a day. Age on 2026-10-26 is 63, which is correct. The cached Britannica page shows 'age 61', but that is a stale snapshot and does not affect the claim.

claims.claim: At nine he arrived in the US with his brother, without his parents, and was placed at Oneida Baptist Institute in Kentucky, a religious reform school for 'difficult' children
claims.note: Britannica says the same. CHM also says he immigrated at age nine.

claims.claim: Birth name Jen-Hsun Huang; father a chemical engineer, mother a primary school teacher
claims.note: Britannica gives 'Jen-Hsun Huang' as the also-known-as name, the father as a chemical engineer and the mother as a grade-school teacher.

claims.claim: At five the family moved to Thailand; the parents did not plan to settle there because of the Vietnam War; his mother taught the boys ten English words a day
claims.note: Britannica says '10 random English words a day'.

claims.claim: The brothers were sent to an uncle in Tacoma, Washington while the parents stayed in Thailand; the uncle enrolled them at Oneida believing it a prestigious boarding school
claims.note: Confirmed.

claims.claim: Huang cleaned toilets daily, his brother worked on a tobacco farm, and both were bullied
claims.note: Confirmed.

claims.claim: About two years later the parents arrived, discovered the situation and withdrew the sons; the family settled in the suburbs of Portland, Oregon
claims.note: Confirmed.

claims.claim: The official NVIDIA profile does not state his birthplace; Britannica and CHM agree on Tainan
claims.note: The NVIDIA bio has no birthplace. Britannica and CHM both say Tainan.

claims.claim: At Aloha High School he played competitive table tennis with a national ranking; finished secondary school in 1981
claims.note: Confirmed.

claims.claim: At Oregon State he studied electrical engineering, met Lori Mills (a fellow engineering student) whom he later married, and graduated in 1984
claims.note: Confirmed. The private-life detail is on the record in Britannica.
The NVIDIA bio gives LSI Logic 1985 to 1993 and AMD 1984 to 1985.

claims.claim: At LSI he rose to run a division; while working he returned to university for a master's in electrical engineering at Stanford
claims.note: Britannica covers the division and the master's earned while working. NVIDIA confirms the MSEE from Stanford.

claims.claim: In April 1993 Huang founded NVIDIA with Chris Malachowsky and Curtis Priem, who picked him as CEO; the aim was GPUs for video games
claims.note: Britannica says April 1993 and that the two selected Huang as CEO. nvidia-history gives 5 April 1993 (not cited in the body, but consistent).

claims.claim: They started with $40,000 in capital and quickly raised $20 million in venture capital
claims.note: Confirmed.

claims.claim: Huang has been president, CEO and board member since the first day
claims.note: The NVIDIA bio says 'since its inception'.

claims.claim: NVIDIA went public in 1999
claims.note: Confirmed.

claims.claim: GeForce 256 launched in 1999; CHM presents it as the first GPU, combining transform, lighting and rendering
claims.note: Confirmed.

claims.claim: At a $100 share price Huang had the NVIDIA logo tattooed on his left shoulder, 'a gesture he says he does not want to repeat'
claims.note: The tattoo, the $100 trigger and the left shoulder are confirmed. Britannica says he would 'most likely' not get another one. The French is slightly firmer than the source's hedge. Softening to 'probablement pas' is optional and does not block approval.

claims.claim: CUDA arrived in 2006 as a platform for general-purpose GPU computing; mid-2000s universities and national labs used NVIDIA chips in some of the fastest supercomputers
claims.note: Confirmed.

claims.claim: In 2012 AlexNet was trained on NVIDIA GPUs and the company pivoted to accelerated computing for AI
claims.note: CHM says so. The NVIDIA timeline also lists 2012 and AlexNet.

claims.claim: At GTC 2018 in San Jose Huang said GPUs were 25x faster than five years earlier, faster than Moore's law; the press dubbed it 'Huang's law'
claims.note: Confirmed.

claims.claim: Late October 2025: first company to pass $5 trillion; stock closed at $207.04, market cap $5.03 trillion
claims.note: Fox Business (30 Oct 2025) gives a close of $207.04 and a market value of $5.03 trillion, and calls Nvidia the first company to reach $5 trillion.

claims.claim: The stock is up 12-fold since ChatGPT's 2022 launch, according to Reuters as reported by Fox Business
claims.note: Confirmed. The attribution is correct.

claims.claim: Fortune Businessperson of the Year 2017; Harvard Business Review No. 1 on its 2019 list of the world's 100 best-performing CEOs over their tenure
claims.note: Confirmed. Britannica agrees on the year and the ranking.

claims.claim: Time included him in 2021 among the 100 most influential people
claims.note: Confirmed.

claims.claim: CHM named him a Fellow in 2024 for graphics, accelerated computing and AI; quote on AI and 'social elevation'
claims.note: The page header reads '2024 Fellow' and the citation text and quote match.

claims.claim: December 2025: Time named the 'Architects of AI' Person of the Year; eight people including Huang, Altman, Su, Musk and Zuckerberg
claims.note: The AP piece is dated 11 Dec 2025 and lists eight leaders including those named.

claims.claim: IEEE awarded him the 2026 Medal of Honor, its highest distinction, for GPU leadership and their application to scientific computing and AI; ceremony in New York in April 2026
claims.note: The ieee-honors page says presented in April 2026 in New York City and calls it IEEE's highest distinction. The citation wording matches ieee-recipient.

claims.claim: The IEEE page also cites his National Academy of Engineering election and the SIA Robert N. Noyce Award
claims.note: Confirmed.

claims.claim: In 2007 Huang and his wife founded the Jen-Hsun and Lori Huang Foundation, which gave to their alma maters, public health initiatives and Bay Area organisations
claims.note: Confirmed.

claims.claim: Summary and knownFor: cofounder, president and CEO of NVIDIA; trained at Oregon State and Stanford; BSEE 1984 and later MSEE; GeForce 256 in 1999; AI pivot after 2012
claims.note: All backed by the body and sources. He still holds the role as of the 2026 sources, so 'dirige depuis' is not outdated.

claims.claim: FAQ: Malachowsky, Priem and Huang founded NVIDIA in April 1993 and Huang was named CEO from the start; BSEE Oregon State 1984 then a Stanford master's while working; born in Tainan, family in Thailand, arrived in the US at nine
claims.note: All consistent with the sources.

claims.claim: Roughly twenty years after arriving in the US he cofounded NVIDIA
claims.note: Arrival around 1972 and founding in 1993 gives about 21 years, so the rounded span is fine.

valueNote: A clear sourced timeline (April 1993 founding, 1999 GeForce, 2012 AI pivot, Oct 2025 $5T, Dec 2025 Time, April 2026 IEEE). It uses primary sources (NVIDIA, CHM, IEEE). It states openly that NVIDIA's own profile gives no birthplace. It answers the age and education queries at the top. The voice is concrete, with no hype words, em dashes or rhetorical openers, and the sections are specifically named. The childhood detail overlaps with Britannica, but the rest is a better-organised timeline than typical results.
summary: I opened all nine sources and checked every claim in the body, summary, knownFor, FAQ and facts. All are confirmed. Dates, ages, company names and years, the Fox Business figures ($207.04 close, $5.03T, 12-fold since ChatGPT per Reuters) and the awards (Fortune 2017, HBR 2019, Time 2021, CHM Fellow 2024, Time 2025, IEEE Medal of Honor 2026 presented April 2026) match. Age 63 on 2026-10-26 is correct. Nothing is outdated and nothing in the body lacks a nearby citation. No net-worth claim appears. One optional polish: the tattoo line says he does not want to repeat it, while Britannica says he would 'most likely' not, so 'probablement pas' would be more exact. The unused sources (nvidia-history, ieee-spectrum) are consistent with the article.
